name: Trichophytic closure
lead: Trichophytic closure is a wound-closure technique used after strip (FUT) donor harvesting in hair transplantation and in facelift incisions. Wound edges are prepared so hair can grow through the scar, helping camouflage it.[1][2]

Published comparisons are small. A 2018 retrospective cohort of 46 rhytidectomy patients compared W-plasty and straight-line trichophytic closure on occipital hairline scars.[3] Other papers describe double or asymmetric suture variants for donor wounds.[4][5]
infobox: FUT donor closure; facelift hairline incisions; scalp scars

paras: Wikipedia says trichophytic closure yields much finer donor scars after strip harvesting.[1] Grokipedia describes a typically fine linear scar about 1 to 2 mm wide.[2] A paper discussed whether "trichophytic" and "pre-trichophytic" closure are different techniques.[6]

Reported variants include double trichophytic closure with wavy two-layered closure,[4] and an asymmetric dermal-subdermal suture for wide donor wounds.[5] Trichophytic closure has also been reported for cicatricial alopecia scars.[7]

A retrospective cohort compared W-plasty and straight-line closure in facelift occipital scars.[3] A registered split-wound study (n=10) compared closure techniques at the hair transplant donor site.[8] Small sample sizes limit these.

card.summary: A suturing method that lets hair grow through the donor scar after strip harvesting; evidence is small comparative studies.
card.note: Applies to strip (FUT) harvesting scars, which remain visible in some cases.

quick.overview:
Trichophytic closure is a way of closing a strip-harvest or facelift incision so hair grows through the scar and hides it.

Studies are small and mostly retrospective.
quick.mechanism: Wound edges are trimmed or stepped so follicles survive at the margin and hair grows through the healing scar.
quick.risks: It is a surgical closure with usual wound risks; scars can still be visible. Reported scar widths come from a general reference.
